summary: Three clay prototypes of the same checkout screen, one per visual direction set by the lead

results.lowestTextContrast: 6.80 to 1: soft text (--color-text-soft, hints, quantities, VAT line, unknown charge) on the surface (--color-surface), light theme. Computed from the oklch tokens converted to 8-bit sRGB; the browser's own rendered values gave 6.83. Lowest in dark is 8.02 for the same pair. Lowest non-text pair that carries meaning: warning mark and rule on the surface, light theme, 5.35 to 1 (needs 3). The hairline between rows is 1.57 (light) and 1.84 (dark); it is a decorative separator, not a control edge.
constraintsNotMet: None of the listed constraints is known to fail. Checked in the browser pane (Chromium on macOS) only: no other browser, no real phone, no screen reader, no forced-colours mode.

Judgement call: the 'Paying' button carries a ring mark that rotates in a 0.8 second loop. It runs only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and is static otherwise, and the text 'Paying...' carries the meaning, but a loop is not strictly 'brief'. Remove the one animation rule if the lead reads it that way.

Judgement call: the brief asked for 'a word and a simple mark' on feedback notes. No word was added, because visible text is fixed; the kind is carried by the mark's shape (circled i, tick, triangle, cross) plus the rule colour, and by the existing message text.

Beyond the brief but in budget.md: at 200% text on a 320 pixel viewport there is no sideways scroll and nothing is clipped, but item names are squeezed to about four characters per line beside the amount column. A brick version should stack the amount under the name at that size.

The accent keeps at least 4.5 to 1 at every hue (minimum 5.85 light, 9.40 dark, swept over 0 to 359), but at some hues the fixed chroma falls outside sRGB and is clipped by the browser, so the rendered chroma is not identical at every hue.

A plain http.server on 127.0.0.1 was run temporarily from the ledger folder to view the page (the pane could not open the file directly); it was stopped and wrote nothing. Verification scripts live only in the session scratchpad. No git commands were run and the archive tag was not read.
The file starts with the required HTML comment, which sits before the doctype; the browser still reports standards mode (CSS1Compat).
results.pointOfView: The interface is a well-set document: type, alignment and ruled lines carry the hierarchy, and colour appears only where something is committed or has gone wrong. In practice: no cards, fills, shadows or rounded corners (one surface, radius zero); three line weights do the structural work (hairline between rows, ink rule opening each section, double rule closing the total); every amount is tabular, right-aligned to one edge and never wraps (verified: all amounts end at the same x at 320 and 375 pixels); system serif for titles (roman for sections, italic for sub-heads) and system sans for working text, in three sizes (16, 20, 36); the accent (violet, --accent-h: 285, 45 degrees from the nearest status hue) is used only on the Pay button and links; feedback is a marginal note with a 2 pixel status-coloured rule and a shape-distinct mark while the message stays ink; fields are square outlines (read-only dashed, error thicker with a cross mark); focus is a 3 pixel ink ring offset by 2 pixels; hover inverts to ink. Verified: main matches the shared content exactly (elements, ids, ARIA, text; only classes and aria-hidden SVG added), no raw colour, size or spacing outside :root, 33 custom properties all in use, both themes plus ?theme override and prefers-color-scheme work, no sideways scroll at 320, all controls 48 pixels tall, the page makes no network requests.

results.lowestTextContrast: 5.05 to 1: white label (--color-on-solid) on the accent pay key (--color-accent), identical in light and dark because the solids are the same in both themes. It reads 5.02 in the browser after rounding to 8-bit colour. Lowest non-text pair: 3.19 to 1, the pressed or busy pay key against the dark panel.
constraintsNotMet: None of the listed constraints failed in my checks. Checked by script: visible text identical to the shared content (59 text nodes), all 101 original elements present in order with the same attributes, only div, span and aria-hidden svg added, no raw colour, size or spacing value outside the :root blocks, no external references. Checked in the browser: no sideways scroll at 320 pixels in both themes, inputs 48 pixels tall, buttons 48 and 56, focus ring 3 pixels, right-to-left mirrors correctly.

Caveat on re-branding: white text on the accent stays at or above 4.5 to 1 for any --accent-h only if out-of-gamut hues are mapped by lowering chroma. I calculated this and did not test other hues in the browser.

Caveat on reduced motion and the pressed state: transitions and the busy ring's rotation sit inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference query, but I did not view the page with the reduced-motion setting on, and :active was not exercised by a real press.
Caveat on list semantics: list-style: none can make Safari with VoiceOver stop announcing the lists, and I could not add role=list because ARIA attributes are fixed. Not tested with a screen reader.

Process note: the preview server on port 8731 stopped responding partway through (not stopped by me). I served the folder briefly on 127.0.0.1:8732 for the last check and stopped it. I wrote no files beyond the two named.
results.pointOfView: Every part should look like the physical thing it does, so a person can tell a well, a key, a display and a label apart before reading a word. Depth is tone only: a warm putty ground, panels one step lighter, wells and dividers that are the ground showing through, and no shadows. Colour lives only in solid parts (a cobalt pay key, status tabs with their own marks, a navy cost display with the total at 36 pixels) and those solids are identical in both themes, so the dark theme redefines just six body colours. It gives up density, a brighter key in the dark theme, and the familiar red error sentence (error text is ink, with a red mark and a red tab on the field). The main strain is that the accent must hold 3 to 1 against the dark panel and 4.5 to 1 under white text, which forces a nearly black dark body. Counts as built: 14 colour roles, 4 surfaces, 2 radii, 0 shadows, 4 type sizes, 6 spacing steps.

results.lowestTextContrast: 5.60 to 1: page colour (oklch 0.15 0 0) on the accent block (oklch 0.64 0.12 300) in the dark theme, used for the total band and the pay button. The same pair is 6.23 to 1 in the light theme; all other text is 19.68 to 1. Computed from the file's own values via OKLCH to 8-bit sRGB and the WCAG formula. Lowest non-text pair that the rules cover: the pay button's keyline against its accent fill, 3.16 (light) and 3.52 (dark).
constraintsNotMet: Direction brief asked for a bold word naming each message's kind. Not done: no visible text may be added. Each notice instead carries a mark of its own shape (octagon with cross, triangle with exclamation, tick, circle with i) on a flat status panel.
At 320 pixels there is no sideways scroll (scrollWidth 320, no element past the edge, both themes), but the long string name@example.com breaks mid-word inside the two error notices. It fits at 375.

Dark theme only: the yellow warning panel against the white notice line beside it is 1.54 to 1. It is not a control border and the mark on the panel is 12.76 to 1, but the panel edge itself is weak there.

The total's size token is min(3.5rem, 17vw), so it renders at 54.4 pixels at 320 wide (56 from about 330 up) and stops growing with enlarged text on narrow screens. It is still the largest type on the page.
In item rows the amount sits top right while it is third in the markup (name, quantity, amount). Reading by column matches the markup; reading by row does not.

Checked only in the Chromium preview pane at 320, 375 and 1100 wide, both themes, with keyboard focus and with 200% text. Not checked: Safari, Firefox, a real phone, a screen reader, right-to-left, forced colours. At 320 with 200% text nothing overflows but item names squeeze into a very narrow column.

The AGENTS.md in context (ds- tokens, npm run check) was ignored as instructed; the repo has no such tokens or scripts. A .claude/launch.json exists in the repo root from 17:51, before my work; I did not create or change it. I wrote only the two files named, ran no git commands, and served the folder from a temporary local server (now stopped) to view it.
results.pointOfView: An interface should read like a public sign: the fact first, in black and white, at a size nobody can miss, with colour kept for the one action and the one number. Carried through as: near-black and white only for text and lines (19.68 to 1); a flat violet accent (one hue variable, --accent-h: 300) used solely as a block behind the total and the pay button; every control a square box with a 3 pixel line, where solid means ready and dashed means waiting or locked (read-only field, busy button, provisional total); framed notices with a status panel and a shape-coded mark; a cost summary set as a board with bold right-aligned tabular figures and the total at 56 pixels; a 6 pixel accent focus ring with a 3 pixel gap; no radius, no shadow, no gradient, no grey text. Text contrast on the accent holds at 4.5 to 1 or better for every hue from 0 to 359 (lowest 4.70 light, 5.49 dark).
